lessons.t: A Great Martyr Ever Cherished (Supplementary Reading)
lessons.au: Edited: Meha Mathur and Tessy Koshy
lessons.words: beckon – call or invite; avert – turn away; surmise – guess; artiste – a professional entertainer; introvert – a person interested in his own thoughts; Casio – a musical keyboard; Sufism – a religious philosophy of prayer, meditation and simple living; exposure – experience or knowledge; ekdam bindas – very carefree; dabbled – tried something without serious commitment; condolence – expression of sympathy; compensation – money given to make up for a loss
lessons.notes: Lieutenant Haneef Uddin – a young army officer who died at the age of 25; Kargil War (1999) – war between India and Pakistan; Sub-sector Haneef – the Turtuk sector named after him; National School of Drama – a theatre institute; Indian Military Academy (IMA) – the army training academy; 11 Rajputana Rifles – his regiment; Haneef Foundation – a foundation set up by his family in Kullu.
ab: Answer the following questions briefly
1. The writer speaks of the ‘smile’ that welcomes anyone who enters Haneef’s house. What more do we know about this smile?
The smile is from a photograph in a picture frame. It belongs to Lieutenant Haneef Uddin, who died at 25, and it is a painful but brave memory.
2. What did Haneef choose as his mission? Why did he do so?

His mission was to ‘change lives’, as shown on a flash card found among his belongings. He joined the army because he knew what he could give to the nation and because he felt his life would be short.
3. Life for Haneef in the beginning was never a smooth sail. Why was it so?
He lost his father at the age of eight, and his mother had to travel often for work, leaving him and his brothers to look after themselves.
4. The absence of his mother from home taught the children something. What was that?
The children became responsible and learned that one’s duty is the most important thing in life.
5. How does the writer describe the introvert Haneef?
He was shy and began to make friends only at 14, but he went out of his way to help people, which gave him joy.
6. Haneef was a young man with varied talents and interests. Illustrate this with support from the text.
He dabbled in art and sketched well, made cards from waste material, read a great deal, loved playing the drums, and formed a music group in his regiment.
Answer the following questions
1. Share your thoughts and impression of Haneef with your classmates.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. Accept personal impressions that refer to his courage, kindness and sense of duty.
2. Imagine you could interview Haneef. Prepare a questionnaire and write his probable replies.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. Check that the questions are polite and relevant, and that the replies match Haneef’s character in the text.

qb.q: The writer speaks of the ‘smile’ that welcomes anyone who enters Haneef’s house. What more do we know about this ‘smile’?
qb.a: The smile that welcomes anyone who enters Haneef’s house gives the memory of a twenty-five-year-old martyr lieutenant HaneefUddin’s painful and brave story.

qb.q: What did Haneef choose as his mission? Why did he do so?
qb.a: Haneef Uddin chose to join the army as his mission because he knew that life was short. Even though who came from a family of musicians, he repeatedly reminded himself of his mission to serve India.

qb.q: Life for Haneef, in the beginning, was never a smooth sail. Why was it so?
qb.a: Life for Haneef in the beginning was never a smooth sail because Hanif lost his father when he was just eight years old. His mother Hema Aziz had to take care of three young boys. But she had to leave the children alone and travel with the performance team of the Information and Broadcasting Ministry.

qb.q: The absence of the mother, from home, taught the children something. What was that?
qb.a: The absence of mother from home taught the children to become responsible, getting up and getting ready for school without having to tell them. It gave the children a message that one’s duty is the most important thing in life.

qb.q: How does the writer describe the ‘introvert’ Haneef?
qb.a: An ‘introvert’ Haneefbegan to make friends only when he was 14 years of age. He would often go out of his way to help people because that gave him a certain kind of joy.

qb.q: Haneef was a young man with varied talents and interests. Illustrate this statement from textual examples.
qb.a: Haneef dabbled in art, sketched very well, made beautiful cards out of waste material, read a great deal and loved playing the drums. That is why the officers at ‘Raj Rifs’ made him get all his instruments from Delhi and form the music group ‘Haneef’.

qb.q: What were the dreams of Haneef? Do you think they were fulfilled?
qb.a: Haneef had dreamt that he would rise up the ranks. This dream could not be fulfilled because he was killed in the Kargil war. Another dream of his was that a post be named after him. This dream came true when a sub-sector was named after him.

qb.q: Why did Haneef become very responsible at his tender age?
qb.a: Haneef lost his father when he was just eight years old. His mother a vocal artist, was out very often with the performance wing. Therefore, he became very responsible at his tender age.

qb.q: How did Haneef’s friends call him? What can we guess from his belongings?
qb.a: Haneef’s friends called him ‘Khalifa’. We can guess from his belongings that he was a true patriot who believed in ‘We change lives”.

qb.q: What were Haneef’s brothers doing at the time of the tragedy?
qb.a: Haneef’s elder brother Nafisuddin went was a teacher at the JD Tyler School, New Delhi. His younger brother was a music composer. Haneef would often team up with him on the drums.

qb.q: How can you say that Haneef was able to reach out to all?
qb.a: Haneef was able to reach out to all. His mother Hema Aziz mentioned that a 77 year-old gentleman, who paid a condolence visit to Haneef’s house, recalled how Haneef had approached him with some queries related to Sufism.

qb.q: How did Haneef come to know about the Indian army?
qb.a: Haneef didn’t know much about the army. The only exposure was that from his mother who was a vocal artist, she often went to perform for the Armed Forces Entertainment Wing.

qb.q: How was the military training at IMA? How did it effect Haneef?
qb.a: According to Haneef the military training at IMA was tough. The trainees had to take a ‘Mussourie bath’ at midnight, which was a cold-water bath at midnight. Through this training, gentle Haneef became a tough army man.

qb.q: How do you say Haneef’s family took the family’s pride to the next l evel even after Haneef’s death?
qb.a: The family started to give scholarship in his name and started a school in Kullu under the Haneef Foundation. His mother politely declined the Indian army’s compensation offer of a petrol pump and suggested to give it to a family whose sole bread-earner was gone.

qb.q: What can we learn from Haneef’s life?
qb.a: We can learn the lesson of self-dependency. We must be ready to sacrifice our lives for the cause of our nation. We must face difficulties boldly. We should have an aim in life. Nation is more important than the individual.

qb.q: What is the present name of Turtuk sector? Why was it renamed?
qb.a: The present name of Turtuk sector in Kargilis Sub sector Haneef. It was renamed in memory of Haneef Uddin’s bravery and dedication in Kargil war.

qb.q: Give a short account of Haneef’s school and college education.
qb.a: Haneef completed his school education in Kerala school, New Delhi. He was graduated from Shivaji College, New Delhi. After his graduation, he had applied to the Indian Army.

qb.q: What compensation was offered to Hema Aziz by the Indian Army? Did she accept it? Give reason.
qb.a: The Indian Army offered a petrol pump as a compensation to Haneef’s mother HemaAziz. But she did not accept. She had the opinion that such compensations must be given to the family whose sole bread earner is gone.

qb.q: Haneef Uddin choose to join the Indian Army to
Haneef Uddin's sacrifice reveals that
o: He valued personal comfort above everything else.
He showed exceptional courage and patriotism.
He was unwilling to face challenges.

qb.q: Haneef Uddin is remembered as a great martyr because
o: He sacrificed his life while defending the country.
He wrote books about the Army.

qb.q: The message, the lesson A Great Martyr Ever Cherished conveys is
o: Wealth is the key to success.
Patriotism and selfless service deserve respect and remembrance.

qb.q: Haneef Uddin inspires the readers the most with his qualities of
o: Courage, dedication, and love for the nation

lessons.words: despite – in spite of; departure – leaving; scree – an area of small loose stones; sole – the bottom surface of a foot; shreds – thin torn pieces; rage – anger; puny – small and weak; reckless – not caring about risk; gouge out – force out an eye; ordeal – suffering; clambered – climbed up with effort; groping – moving in the dark with the hands; crawl – move slowly on hands and knees; defiantly – refusing to obey; howled – cried loudly like a wolf; boundless – without limit; rumbling – making a low sound of hunger; caressed – touched gently with love; bloomed – flowered; chorus – singing together; mountain peach – mountain fruit
lessons.notes: Tibet – a region of Asia known for its mountains; barley wine and barley grains – Tibetan customs of wishing a good journey; The Bird of Happiness – a symbol of real happiness; Lousang, Silong, Bhima – names of people in the story whom the monsters ask Wangjia to harm.
ab: Think about the text

Source of happiness (pre-reading): complete the boxes – Speaking …; Showing sympathy for …; Being … to others; Living in tune with …; Acquiring … qualities; Thinking of … . Can you give examples to prove your point?

ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. ಮಾದರಿ: Speaking kindly; showing sympathy for the poor; being helpful to others; living in tune with nature; acquiring good qualities; thinking of others’ welfare.
1. ‘Will I ever make it?’ Why did Wangjia feel so?
He faced terrible hardships on the scree and in hunger and blindness, and he was not sure he could reach the Bird of Happiness.
2. What hardships did Wangjia undergo on his way to find the Bird?
His boots were ripped, his feet were cut, his hands were torn, he was starved, his bread-bag was blown away, and his eyes were forced out so that he became blind. He had to crawl.
3. What changes came over Wangjia as the Bird caressed him?
His eyeballs returned to their sockets, he could see more brightly than before, his wounds were healed, and he became stronger than ever.
4. What contrast do you draw between the monsters’ wishes and Wangjia’s wish? What does the folktale suggest?

The monsters wanted him to harm others: to kill, poison or blind innocent people, so their wishes were selfish and cruel. Wangjia wished for warmth and happiness for his people and refused to harm anyone. The story suggests that real happiness comes from kindness and from living in harmony with others.
5. Read paragraph 1 and paragraphs 28 and 29. What do you understand about real happiness?
Real happiness is not wealth but warmth, forests, fields, rivers and flowers, that is, a life lived in harmony with nature and with others, free from hardship.
6. What do you like the most in the story? Support your answer with reasons.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. Accept reasoned answers that refer to Wangjia’s courage or the message about kindness.
7. Discuss with your partner and fill in the table: the first, second and third monster’s action and Wangjia’s answer or challenge.

First monster: asked Wangjia to kill Lousang’s mother; turned the road into sharp scree; Wangjia refused: ‘I’ll never kill another person’s.’ Second monster: asked him to poison old gaffer Silong; blew away his bread-bag and made a desert; Wangjia refused: ‘I’m fond of my own grandpa.’ Third monster: asked him to bring Bhima’s eyeballs; blinded him when he refused; Wangjia refused: ‘No one has the right to destroy a girl’s pretty eyes.’

8. Which ways of achieving happiness are practicable and which are impracticable? (a) working hard to satisfy everybody’s wants (b) giving up all selfish desires (c) striking a balance between selfishness and sacrifice (d) working together for the good of all (e) leading a simple contented life (f) devoting some time of the day for the good of others
Practicable: c, d, e, f. Impracticable: a (it is impossible to satisfy everybody’s wants) and b (giving up all desires is hard for most people). Accept reasoned discussion.

qb.q: Why were the people of Tibet unhappy?
qb.a: A certain village in Tibet was very poor. It had no rivers or good land, no warmth or fresh flowers. People suffered from hunger and cold all year around. So, they were unhappy.

qb.q: What did the old folk of Tibet say about happiness?
qb.a: The old folk used to say that happiness was a beautiful bird. It lived in a snowy mountain far away in the East. Wherever the bird flew, happiness went with it.

qb.q: Who was selected to find the bird of happiness? What was done on his departure?
qb.a: Wangjia, a bright boy was selected to find the bird of happiness. On his departure, the girls of the village offered him barley wine and the mothers spread barley grains on his head to wish him a good journey.

qb.q: What did the first monster ask Wangjia to do? How did Wangjia react to it?
qb.a: The first monster told Wangjia to kill Lousang’s mother if he wanted to see the bird of happiness. Wangjia replied that he loved his own mother and would never kill another person’s mother.

qb.q: How did the first old monster punish Wangjia? “Will I ever make it?” Why did Wangjia feel so?
qb.a: When Wangjia was not ready to kill Lousang’s mother, the first monster began to blow his long beard. Immediately, the smooth road became a vast scree. Wangjia had to walk on a stony path. Every stone was as sharp as a knife. His boots got torn, his feet got cut and his hands torn to shreds. At that time, he wondered if he would ever make it.

qb.q: How did Wangjia react to the second monster?
qb.a: The second monster asked Wangjia to poison his enemy old gaffer Sillong. Wangjia was fond of his own grandpa and he would never kill another man’s grandpa.

qb.q: How did the second monster make Wangjia suffer?
qb.a: The second monster blew through his beard and Wangjia’s bread bag flew into the air. The mountains and rivers turned into a vast desert with no food to be found. Wangjia’s stomach rumbled, head swam and as he went further, he felt a shooting pain in his stomach due to hunger.

qb.q: What did the third monster warn Wangjia? How did Wangjia respond?
qb.a: The third monster told Wangjia to bring Bhima’s eyeballs and if he refused, he would take out Wangjia’s eyeballs. Wangjia responded that he would not do itas no one had the right to destroy a pretty girl’s eyes.

qb.q: How was the third journey difficult for Wangjia?
qb.a: When Wangjia refused to bring Bhima’s eyeballs, the third monster made him blind. Groping his way with his hands on the ground, he had to crawl another nine hundred miles.

qb.q: What contrast do you draw between the wishes of the monsters and the wish of Wangjia?
qb.a: All the three monsters wanted to harm others. On the other hand, Wangjia wished to make the people of his land happy. Though the monsters troubled Wangjia, he bravely faced all the difficulties. His wish came true and finally good won over the evil.

qb.q: What do you like the most in the story? Support your answer giving reasons.
qb.a: The best part of the story is patience, selflessness and courage shown by Wangjia bravely. He refused to perform the evil deeds they asked him to do. He was suffered by the punishments given by the monsters but did not lose his hope. Hence, he was able to bring back the happiness to his village.

qb.q: What hardships did Wangjia undergo on his way to find the bird?
qb.a: Wangjia came across three monsters on his way. Each of them gave him an inhuman task. He refused to do them.So, the first monster changed a smooth road into a vast scree. Walking on that road, Wangjia’s boots got torn, his feet were cut to pieces, his hands were torn to shreds. The second monster turned everything into a desert with no food at all. Wangjia felt hungry. His head swam and he had a sharp pain in the stomach. The third monster blew his beard and Wangjia’s eye balls jumped out of the sockets and he became blind. Groping his way, Wangjia finally reached the top of the mountain and found the bird of happiness.

qb.q: How did the Bird of happiness put an end to the hardships suffered by the people?
qb.a: Standing on the mountain top the bird of happiness gave three loud cries. At the first cry,the golden sun appeared through the clouds and the warm breeze began to blow. At the second cry, the mountains were covered with forests. Flowers began to bloom and birds started singing. At the third cry, green fields and rivers appeared and white rabbits danced merrily on the grass. From that day onwards, the people never suffered hardships again.

qb.q: What changes came over Wangjia as the bird of happiness caressed him?
qb.a: The bird of happiness caressed Wangjia gently with its wings and sang for him. His eyeballs flew back to their sockets and he could see much more brightly than before. All his wounds were healed and he was stronger than ever. The bird offered him some dried meat and cream cake and then bore him back his village.

qb.q: How can you say that Wangjia was a brave boy?
qb.a: Wangjia had two ways to find the bird of happiness. He never chose the easy way by killing enemies of the monsters. He rejected the wishes of the monsters politely and obeyed the most difficult tasks given by them. Whenever he thought of his village people, he forgot all his sufferings. Due of his courage, patience and love towards his people, he was able to find the bird of happiness and succeed in bringing back happiness to his village.

qb.q: In what way was the bird of happiness guarded?
qb.a: The Bird of Happiness was guarded by three old monsters,who could kill a man by simply blowing through their long beards. Every year people of Tibet went to look for this bird but not one of them did ever return.

qb.q: Why do you think the people of Tibet offered Wangjia a number of things?
qb.a: The people offered Wangjia many things because they knew his journey would be long, difficult, and dangerous. He had to face three powerful monsters to bring back the Bird of Happiness. They gave him food, barley wine and other useful items to help him on his journey. They also wished for his success and hoped he would return safely with the Bird of Happiness.

qb.q: Why did Wangjia decide not to go back from his journey?
qb.a: After the first stage of his journey, Wanjia felt that it was tough going. He wondered whether he would succeed in finding the bird of happiness. However he did not loose courage and thinking of turning back. He reminded himself that the people in his village were waiting for him to bring back happiness. So he continued his journey.

qb.q: In which direction did Wangjia start to walk and why? Study the following picture and answer the questions from 1 to 5 based on the lesson ‘The Bird Of Happiness.’( 4 marks)
qb.a: Wangjia started to work eastwards for many days until he saw a large mountainbecause he knew that the Bird of Happiness lives on a snowy mountain in the east.

qb.q: Wangjia decided to search for the Bird of Happiness
o: To help the suffering people of his village

qb.q: To show courage while facing the three old monsters, Wangjia
o: asked others to fight for him.
faced them fearlessly to complete his mission.

qb.q: The quality of Wangjia that inspires the readers, the most is
Wangjia's journey teaches us that
o: We should think only about ourselves.
We should act with courage and kindness for the welfare of others.
We should expect rewards for every good deed.

qb.q: The statement that best describes Wangjia's character is
o: He was a brave and kind-hearted boy who risked his life to bring happiness to others.
He was afraid of every challenge.
He wanted only wealth and power.
He depended entirely on others for help

lessons.au: Shanta Rameshwar Rao (poem: Carl Wendall Hines Jr – “Jazz Poem Two”)
lessons.words: maestro – a great performer, especially a musician; excited – feeling happiness and enthusiasm; sprang – moved quickly and suddenly; with a catch in her throat – with a feeling of great sorrow; unbidden – without being asked; self-reproach – blame against oneself; gravely – seriously; pretend – act in a way to make others believe something untrue; astonishment – a feeling of great surprise; miracle – an event that does not follow the laws of nature; hung in the air – was worrying everyone; choked – filled with sadness; enchantment – a feeling of great pleasure; ovation – enthusiastic clapping by the audience; wriggle – twist and turn the body with quick movements; wizard – a person who is especially good at an art; bother – trouble or worry; solitude – the state of being alone; ears perk – brighten up; gospel – religious music sung loudly; screaming notes – loud musical sounds; wearies of living – no longer interested in life; fray – threads starting to come apart; sag – to hang down
lessons.notes: Pandit Ravi Shankar – an Indian sitar musician and composer; Ustad Allah Rakha – an Indian tabla player who often accompanied Pandit Ravi Shankar; Ancient Mariner – a reference to Coleridge's poem ‘The Rime of the Ancient Mariner’, in which a seaman shoots an albatross and suffers supernatural punishment; Jazz – a style of music with improvisation and strong rhythm; The story is a true one; all names except Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Allah Rakha have been changed.
ab: Before you read
a. Can you identify the person in this picture?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. ಮಾದರಿ: The picture shows a singer performing with a microphone. The book does not name him, so accept the student’s reasoned guess.
images/class-10/english/c10-en-l05-singer-photo.webp
b. Look at the picture closely. How does it strike you? Can you describe his feelings from the expression on his face?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. ಮಾದರಿ: He looks deeply absorbed and emotional, as if he is pouring his heart into the song.
images/class-10/english/c10-en-l05-singer-photo.webp
Music is a source of imagination. Reason for choice: music is a source of imagination. Complete: Music gives me / tells me / makes me / For me music is…
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. ಮಾದರಿ: Music tells me stories; for me music is peace.
Check your understanding (Paragraphs 1–4)
1. Which word in the first paragraph describes the manner of the girl when she saw the newspaper?
excitedly.
2. Why do you think the mother cautioned the girl?
The mother cautioned her because the boy was seriously ill and needed all the sleep and rest he could get.
3a. What chance did the boy not like to miss? Why?
He did not want to miss the chance to hear and see Pandit Ravi Shankar, whom he had always wanted to see and hear.
3b. Do you think the boy would get a chance in future?
Probably not. He was very ill and was not expected to recover, so the chance was unlikely to come again.
4. Imagine you were the mother of the boy. Would you have reacted differently? If so, how?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. Accept reasoned answers. ಮಾದರಿ: I would have calmed him gently and tried to find a way for him to hear the music at home.
5. What does ‘a catch in her throat’ suggest about the boy’s condition?
It suggests that the boy was very weak. He could raise himself only with great effort, which shocked and moved his mother. In paragraph 4 he begins to cough and gasp for breath and needs oxygen.
Check your understanding (Paragraphs 5–9)
1. For a moment, Smita had forgotten something. What was it?
She had forgotten that her brother Anant was very ill.
2. In what way was the truth frightening to Smita?
The truth was that Anant was dying of cancer and had not many days to live.
3. Do you consider Anant a talented boy? Justify with support from the text.
Yes. He was the best table-tennis player and the fastest runner in his school, he was better than Smita at the sitar, and he could compose his own tunes to the astonishment of their guru.
4a. What were their ‘high hopes’?
They hoped Anant would be cured at the hospital, walk and run again, take part in the table-tennis tournament, and become a great sitarist.
4b. Do you think their hopes would be fulfilled? Support your answer.
Unlikely. The doctors told them to take Anant home and give him whatever he liked, which showed that his condition was hopeless.
4c. Doctors said something to the parents. Were those words of hope or words of despair? (Para 6)
Words of despair.
4d. ‘They did not voice their fears.’ Who does ‘they’ stand for? i) doctors ii) friends iii) family members
iii) family members.
5. ‘Her eyes filled with tears’. Were they tears of happiness or sorrow? Give reasons.
Tears of sorrow. Smita was sad about her brother’s illness and the fact that he could not go to the concert with her.
6. ‘Suddenly a daring thought came to her’. Can you guess what thought Smita had?
She thought of going to the concert after all, since there was no harm in trying, so that she could hear Pandit Ravi Shankar. Then she planned to ask the musicians to come and play for her brother.
Check your understanding (Paragraphs 10–16)
1. The word ‘gasp’ suggests surprise or pain. Which meaning is relevant in this context? (Para 10)
Pain. The words came out in painful gasps.
2. As Smita sat listening to the music, she was spellbound. But all the while, her mind was echoing something else. What was that?
Her mind was echoing Anant’s words, ‘The chance of a lifetime’, and her plan to ask the musicians to play for him.
3. Why does the writer use the word ‘wriggled’ to describe Smita’s movement?
Smita was small and had to push and twist through the crowd to reach the stage.
4. Identify two more phrases in the next paragraph that describe a state similar to ‘her heart beating loudly’.
‘Her knees felt weak’ and ‘her tongue dry’.
5. Did Smita tell the musicians what she had in her mind? Who responded immediately? What was the response?
Yes, she told them about her brother. Ustad Allah Rakha responded at once, agreeing to perform for the boy the next morning.
6. Do you think the response of the artists was unusual? If yes, why?
Yes. Great artists do not usually perform at a private home on such short notice, especially for a sick child.
7. The neighbours could not believe their eyes. Why do you think they felt like this?
Two of the greatest musicians of the country were getting out of a taxi outside their building. It seemed impossible.
8. Read the last paragraph and exchange your feelings with your partner.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. Accept personal responses that refer to the emotion of the last paragraph.
9. Can you say that the concert was entertaining to Smita? Justify your answer.
Yes. She was spellbound and felt the gates of enchantment opening. However, her mind stayed on her brother’s words, so she was not fully entertained.
10. Smita was nervous as she stood before the wizard. Which sentence suggests this?
‘Her knees felt weak, her tongue dry.’
11. Did Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Allah Rakha perform in the boy’s house? Do you think this was an unusual incident? If yes, give reasons.
Yes, they did. It was unusual because such famous musicians rarely perform in a private home. They did it out of kindness for a dying boy.
Think about the text
1. Do you like the story? Why?
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. ಮಾದರಿ: I like the story because it shows the power of music, kindness and the strong wish of a sick boy.
2. Which words describe Anant’s character or state? Write Yes/No. (a) energetic (b) robust (c) aesthetic (d) imaginative (e) confident
a) energetic – Yes; b) robust – No, he is weak now; c) aesthetic – Yes, he loves music; d) imaginative – Yes, he composes his own tunes; e) confident – Yes.
3. Categorise the phrases in columns A and B. (spellbound; unfolding the gates of enchantment; plaintive notes; fast twinkling ones; first notes; wonder; dream; unfolding ragas)

1. Read the first stanza and fill in the table: Face – wrinkled old face, full of the wearies of living; Eyes – closed; Shirt – frayed-collar, faded-blue old shirt, dark with sweat; Necktie – old, undone; Jacket – worn old jacket; Shoes – run-down, with paper in them.
Face: wrinkled old face; Eyes: closed; Collar and shirt: frayed-collar, faded-blue old shirt; Necktie: old, undone; Jacket: worn; Shoes: run-down, with paper in them.
2. Why do you think the Jazz player keeps his head down? [lines 1–6]
He is lost in his music and in his own solitude, and he is weary of life, so he keeps his head down with closed eyes.
3. The word ‘old’ has been repeated several times in the first two stanzas. What does this suggest?
It suggests the age, weariness and long hardships of the musician’s life.
4. What description do the lines 13 to 18 suggest about the Jazz player?
They suggest poverty and neglect: his sagging stomach, rough unshaven face showing pain, and shoes with paper in them show a hard and poor life.
5a. Read the lines 19 to 25. Is there any change in the stature of the Jazz player?
Yes. He stands firm and self-absorbed, with his ears perked and trained on the bass line, so he appears more composed and focused.
5b. Read the lines 31 to 35. What is he meditating on?
He is meditating on his identity as a Black man and the message he wants to preach to the world through the Black Gospel of Jazz.
6. How has he held his instrument?
He gently lifts the old alto saxophone to his parted lips. It is supported from his neck by a wire coat hanger.

‘It’ stands for the Black Gospel of Jazz, the message of the musician.
9. ‘He is no longer a man’, says the poet (line 37). Who else is he supposed to be?
He is supposed to be a bird that gathers his wings and flies high and away.
10. Read the last ten words of the poem. You may observe a change in the tone. What is that about?
The tone changes from admiration to a sad, realistic note. The musician must return to being a Black man in everyday life, which is a painful reality.

qb.a: Anant’s family stayed with Aunt Sushila in Bombay. Her apartment was not big but there was always room for them.

qb.q: Why had Smitha and her family come to Bombay? Who did they stay with, there?
qb.a: Whenever Smita’s family came to Bombay for Anant’s treatment, they stayed in aunt Sushila’s house. Her apartment was small but there was always room for them. By this, we can say that aunt Sushila was a generous lady.

qb.q: ‘They had come with high hopes’. What hopes did Anant’s parents have?
qb.a: Anant’s parents had come with hopes in the miracles of modern science. They hoped that Anant would be cured in the hospital. He would again walk and run and even take part in the table tennis tournament. He would play the sitar and would be a great sitarist one day.

qb.q: What did the doctors say to Anant’s parents? Why?
qb.a: The doctors at the cancer hospital asked the parents to take the boy home and give him the things he liked and indulge him. It is because his condition grew worse each passing day.

qb.q: How did Anant’s family members treat him without ‘voicing their fears’?
qb.a: Anant’s family members laughed and smiled and talked and surrounded Anant with whatever made him happy. They fulfilled his every need and gave whatever he asked for.

qb.q: Anant expressed his desire of going to the concert. How did his mother pacify him?
qb.a: Mother told her son Anant that she would take him to the concert after he recovered from his illness. She also told him that Pandit Ravishankar would be visiting Bombay again and this would not be the last time.

qb.q: ‘Smitha’s eyes filled with tears’. Were they tears of happiness or sorrow? Give reasons.
qb.a: They are definitely tears of sorrow. When her brother said that the opportunity of hearing Pandit Ravi Shankar wasa chance of a lifetime, her eyes filled with tears, thinking that he would miss the chance, due to his condition.

qb.q: Why did aunt Sushila suggest a walk in the park to Smita?
qb.a: Smita was feeling bad as her brother was too sick to attend the concert. She could not take him with her. So, her aunt suggested her to take a walk in the park to feel better.

qb.q: ‘Suddenly a daring thought came to her’. Can you guess what thought Smita had?
qb.a: The daring thought that Smitha got was to fulfil herbrother’s wish of listening to Pandit Ravi Shankar. Smita planned to request the artists to come to her house and play the sitar for her brother.

qb.q: What was the intention of Smita’s going to the concert?
qb.a: Smitha’s intention of going to the concert was to request Pandit Ravishankar to come to her house and play for her brother Anant. She wanted to fulfil her brother’s wish.

qb.q: How did Smitha enjoy the concert?
qb.a: The concert was entertaining to Smita. The first notes came over the air, and Smitha felt as if the gates of enchantment and wonder were opening. She had listened to music in a spellbound state.

qb.q: Smita was nervous as she stood before the artists. Illustrate this statement from the lesson, ‘The Concert’.
qb.a: Smita was nervous as she stood before the wizard. The sentence ‘Her knees felt weak, her tongue dry’ suggests this.

qb.q: What did the moustachioed man tell Smitha? How did Pandit Ravi Shankar react to it?
qb.a: The moustachioed man told Smitha that Pandit Ravi Shankar was a busy man. He asked her not to bother him with such requests. Ravi Shankar motioned him to be quiet.

qb.q: Ustad Sahib and Pandit Ravi Shankar agreed to perform for the boy. What made them agree to do so?
qb.a: After the concert, Smita went up to the stage and approached Pandit Ravishankar. She explained the condition and the wish of her brother. The musicians were touched by her brother’s story and agreed to perform for the boy.

qb.q: The neighbours of Aunt Sushila could not believe their eyes. Why do you think they felt like this?
qb.a: The neighbours could not believe their eyes, as Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Allah Rakha were very famous artists and very busy. Here were such great persons who came to common people’s apartment to give a concert.

qb.q: What was Smitha's plan to help her brother?
qb.a: Smitha's plan was to request Pandit Ravishankar to play the sitar for her brother. After the concert she went up the stage, approached him and explained her brother’s condition and wish to him. They agreed and came to her house and fulfilled Anant’s last wish.

qb.q: Why did Smita request Pandit Ravi Shankar to visit her house?
qb.a: Smitha’s brother Anant had a wish to see and hear Pandit Ravi Shankar. But he could not go to the concert with her sister because he was suffering from cancer and was bedridden. To fulfil her brother’s wish Smitha requested Ravi Shankar to play the sitar for her brother.

qb.q: What makes the readers appreciate Pandit Ravishankar and Ustad Allah Rakha?
qb.a: Pandit Ravishankar and Ustad Allah Rakha were great maestros. They were busy people. Despite their busy schedule, they accepted Smita’s invitation. They visited Anant’s house and played for him and fulfilled his last wish. Indeed, it was a good example for generosity and humanity of great artists.

qb.q: How did Pandit Ravishankar and Ustad Allah Rakha keep their promise to Smitha? Read the following extracts and answer the questions that follow: ( 3 marks)
qb.a: After listening Smitha’s story about her brother Pandit Ravi Shankar and ustad Allah Rakha were moved. They promised to play for the boy. The next day they came to Smitha’s house and played for her brother and fulfilled his last wish.

qb.q: “You’ll wake him up. You know he needs all the sleep and rest he can get”. a) Who is the speaker? b) Who does ‘you’ refer to? c) Who needed rest? d) Why did he need rest?
qb.a: a) Smitha’s mother b) Smitha c) Ananth d) Anant was suffering from cancer and he was bedridden.

qb.q: “We mustn’t miss the chance” a) Who said these words? b) What chance did the boy not want to miss? c) Why would the boy, not get a chance in the future?
qb.a: a) Ananth b) Attending Pandit Ravishankar’s music concert. c) The boy was suffering from cancer and he was bedridden.

qb.q: “I must hear him and see him” a) Who is the ‘I’? b) Who did the speaker want to see? c) What did the speaker want to hear?
qb.a: a) Anant b) Pandit Ravi Shankar c) He wanted to hear the sitar concert of Pandit Ravishankar.

qb.q: ‘It’s the chance of a lifetime.’ a) Who made this statement? b) What was the chance of a lifetime? c) Why did the speaker say so?
qb.a: a) Ananth b) To see and hear Pandit Ravi Shankar was the chance of a lifetime c)He was a great fan of Pandit Ravishankar, a sitar maestro.

qb.q: “They had come with high hopes” a) Who does ‘they’ refer to? b) Where had they come? c) What high hopes did they have?
qb.a: a) Smitha and her parents b) Bombay c) That Ananth would be cured and would walk and play as before.

qb.q: “Take him home. Give him the things he likes, indulge him” a) Who said the above statement? b) Who does ‘him’ refer to? c) Why was this statement made?
qb.a: a) Doctors who were treating Ananth. b) Anant c) Ananth’s condition grew worse with each passing day and the doctors knew that the boy had not many days to live.

qb.q: “But they did not voice their fears” a) Who does the word ‘they’ stand for? b) What did Ananth’s parents fear? c) How did they behave towards him?
qb.a: a) Ananth’s family members b) Ananth’s parents feared that the boy had not many days to live. c) They laughed and talked and surrounded Anant with whatever made him happy. They fulfilled his every need.

qb.q: “The chance of a lifetime,” he was saying. (a) Who does ‘he’ refer to? (b) What was the chance of a lifetime for him? (c) Why was he feeling so?
qb.a: a) Anant b) Attending Pandit Ravi Shankar’s concert. c) He was a great fan of Pandit Ravishankar, a sitar maestro.

qb.q: ‘’This is not the last time they are going to play’’ a) Who said this and to whom? b) Who was going to play and what? c) When did the speaker say these words?
qb.a: a) Anant’s mother said these words to Anant. b) Pandit Ravi Shankar was going to play the sitar. c) Anant wished to go to Pandit Ravi Shankar’s concert

qb.q: ‘’Your father will take you.’’ a) Who is the speaker, here? b) Who does ‘you’ refer to? c) Where would the father take the listener? d) When did the speaker say so?
qb.a: a) Smitha’s mother b) Smitha c) Father would take her to the concert. d) Smitha felt sad because Ananth would not go with her to the concert and she had to go alone.

qb.q: “No, how can I? We’ve always done things together”. a) Who is the speaker? b) Who does ‘we’ refer to? c) What did they do together? d) What is the speaker refusing to do now?
qb.a: a) Smitha b) Ananth and Smitha c) Because Anant was suffering from cancer and he was bedridden.

qb.q: A walk in the park might make you feel better” a) Who gave this suggestion? b) Who does ‘you’ refer to? c) Why did the speaker say this?
qb.a: a) Aunt Sushila b) Smitha c)Because Smitha was very sad and much worried about her brother’s health.

qb.q: ‘’Suddenly a daring thought came to her’’ a) Where was the speaker when she got the daring thought? b) Who does ‘her’ refer to? c) What was her daring thought?
qb.a: a) In the park. b) Smitha c) She thought of requesting Pandit Ravi Shankar to come to her house and play the sitar for her brother.

qb.q: “There is no harm in trying it” a) Who said these words? b) What is the ‘it’? c) What was the result of trying it?
qb.a: a) Smitha b) Requesting Pandit Ravi Shankar to come to her house and play the sitar for her brother. c) Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Allah Rakha agreed to come to her house and play for her brother.

qb.q: “Enjoy yourself, lucky you!” a) Who is the speaker? b) Who is the ‘you’? c) Why did the speaker consider the listener, lucky?
qb.a: a) Ananth b) Smitha. c) Ananth could not go because of his ill health while Smith could attend the concert,

qb.q: “Panditji is a busy man. You must not bother him with such requests” a) Who said this? b) Who does ‘you’ refer to? c) What was the request? d) Who is the moustachioed man? e) Why did the listener come there?
qb.a: a) A large moustachioed man. b) Smitha c) Smitha requested Pandit Ravi Shankar to come to her house and play for Ananth. d)the organiser of the concert.

qb.q: ‘’What shall we do Ustad Sahib?’’ a) Who asked this question? b) Who was Ustad Sahib? c) When did the speaker say these words?
qb.a: a) Pandit Ravi Shankar b) Tabla master c) Smitha requested Pandit Ravi Shankar to come to her house and play for her dying brother.

qb.q: “Tomorrow morning we perform for the boy” a) Who would perform for the boy? b) Why would they perform? c) What was the result?
qb.a: a) Pandit Ravi Shankar and -Ustad Allah Rakha b) Because they understood the boy’s pathetic condition and wish. c) The boy enjoyed the performance and breathed his last.

qb.q: “Did you hear him?”, he asked. a) Who asked this question? b) Who is the ‘him’? c) What reply did the speaker get?
qb.a: a) Ananth b) Pandit Ravi Shankar c) Smitha told Ananth that Ravi Shankar would come to her house the next day and play.

qb.q: “I spoke to him and he’ll come tomorrow morning’’ a) Who is the ‘I’? b) Who did the ‘I’ speak to? c) What was spoken to him? d) Why would he come the next morning?
qb.a: a) Smitha b) Pandit Ravi Shankar c) Smitha told Ravi Shankar about her brother’s condition and wish and requested him to come to her house and play for her brother. d) To play sitar for her sick bother.

qb.q: They could not believe their eyes. “It is… It’s not possible” they said. a) Who is referred to as ‘they’? b) What was not possible for them to believe? c) Why did they feel so?
qb.a: a) The neighbours of aunt Sushila. b) The fact that Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Allah Rakha had come to aunt Sushila’s house to play for Ananth. c) Because Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Allah Rakha were great musicians and busy people.

qb.q: In the course of the story whom do you consider to be more worried, Smita or Anant? Explain.
qb.a: In my opinion Smitha was very much worried about Anant’s condition and wish. Anant was suffering from cancer and he was bedridden. When he came to know about Pandit Ravishankar's concert, he wanted to see him and hear him. Smitha had great love and affection for her brother Anant. Both of them always did the work together. She was very much worried because she had to go to the concert without him. Finally, she decided to go to the concert to request Pandit Ravishankar to play for her brother. The maestros were moved by the story of Anant and promised her that they would come to her house and play for Anant.

qb.q: Why do you think Smitha and Pandit Ravi Shankar deserve the appreciation?
qb.a: Smitha and her brother Anant were great fans of Pandit Ravishankar. Smitha came to know that there was a concert by Ravi Shankar. She could not take Anant with her because he was suffering from cancer and he was bedridden. Finally, Smitha decided to go to the concert to fulfil her brother’s wish. After enjoying the concert, she requested Pandit Ravishankar to come to her house and play for her brother. No one could imagine that a great musician like Pandit Ravi Shankar would accept her request. He accepted her invitation and played for the boy. Anant enjoyed the performance and breathed his last,peacefully. By this we can say that both Smitha and Ravi Shankar deserve the appreciation.

qb.q: Read the paragraph and answer the questions that follow: (4 marks) One morning in a small apartment in Bombay, a girl of about sixteen looked up fromthe newspaper she was reading and said excitedly, “Pandit Ravi Shankar is playing tomorrow at the Shanmukhananda Auditorium!”“Sh-sh,” said her mother, pointing to the boy lying on the bed. “You’ll wake him up. You know he needs all the sleep and rest he can get.”But the boy on the bed was not asleep. “Pandit Ravi Shankar!” he said. “The sitar maestro! I must hear him... It's the chance of a lifetime!” He tried to raise himself on his elbows but fell back, exhausted. His eyes shone with excitement.They had come to Bombay from Gaganpur so that he could be treated at the cancer hospital. Whenever they thought of him, they thought of his many talents. He was the fastest runner in the school and the best table-tennis player. And he had already started learning to play the sitar; they were both learning it. But now, he was struck by this terrible disease. 1. The Sitar maestro who was going to perform in Bombay was A. Ustad Bismillah Khan B. Pandit Ravi Shankar C. Pandit Shivkumar Sharma D. Ustad Allah Rakha 2. The mother tried to tell the girl to keep quiet ("Sh-sh") as A. She did not want to listen to the musical news B. She was busy doing the household chores. C. She wanted her sick son, to get enough sleep and rest. D. She was reading an important school book. 3. According to Anant, attending the concert was a "the chance of a lifetime" because A. tickets were available for free. B. he wanted to travel around Bombay. C. he was a great admirer of Pandit Ravi Shankar D. his school had sponsored the trip. 4. Anant's family moved from Gaganpur to Bombay ion order to A. buy a new house in the city. B. get treatment for Anant's cancer at a hospital. C. attend music concerts every week. D. admit Anant to a better sports school. 5. The statement that is TRUE about Anant's talents, before he fell ill is A. He was a singer and a cricket player. B. He was a talented sitar player, a fast runner, and a table-tennis player. C. He was a violinist and a famous painter. D. He was a writer and loved playing football.
qb.a: 1. B)Pandit Ravi Shankar 2.C) She wanted her sick son, Anant, to get enough sleep and rest. 3.C )Because he was a great admirer of Pandit Ravi Shankar and played the sitar himself. 4.B) To get treatment for Anant's cancer at a hospital. 5.B) He was a talented sitar player, a fast runner, and a top table-tennis player.

lessons.words: assumed assiduity – pretended interest; rigging – ropes and sails of a ship; mutinous – rebellious; pumping – encouraging someone to talk; surlily – rudely; ruddy – pink and healthy; melancholy – very sad; vision – forethought; descend – move from a higher to a lower level; unbridled – uncontrolled; appeased – satisfied; blight – a curse; poop – the high deck at the back of a ship; startle – frighten or surprise suddenly; reluctantly – unwillingly; whimsically – in an amusing way; humouring – liking, indulging; surge – rise and fall forcefully; ominous – suggesting something bad is about to happen; carcass – dead body; transfixed – stopped, not able to move; helm – wheel for steering a ship; wont – habit; discretion – ability to do right thinking; in irons – chained; froth and scum – silly talk; renegade – traitor; stampede – sudden rush of people; whelp – dog, a rude word for a person; radiant – bright; dominion – land to be owned; redeem – get back; sheepish – meek, embarrassed; deliberation – careful thought; heave to – stop a ship; delirious – almost mad with joy; ballad – narrative poem in rhythmic verse for singing; tempest – violent storm; shudder – shake; stout – brave; stagger – walk unsteadily; anchor – metal device to hold a ship in place; harbour – shelter for ships; breakers – large waves moving towards land
lessons.notes: Christopher Columbus – Italian navigator who sailed for Spain and reached the New World on 11 October 1492; Santa Maria – Columbus’s ship; Pedro Gutierrez – an officer; Pepe – a page-boy; Diego Garcia, Juan Patino, Guillermo Ires, Francisco – seamen; Ferdinand II and Isabella I – the Spanish King and Queen who sponsored the voyage; maravedis – old Spanish coin; Swami Vivekananda – Indian thinker quoted in the exercises; ‘Fortune favours the brave’ – a well-known saying; The Three Voices – a poem by Robert William Service.

Before you read – Three types of people
1. Classify the qualities into the Can’s, the Can'ts and the Won’ts.

Can’s: 1 (always confident of their ability), 5 (spirited and determined), 8 (fit to rule, they think), 10 (nothing can stop them), 12 (optimistic).
Can'ts: 2 (too weak to take up the challenge), 6 (overruled by the consequences), 9 (lack confidence), 11 (always say it is impossible).
Won'ts: 3 (able but unwilling), 4 (like risk-free jobs), 7 (lazy and easily satisfied).
2. Exchange your list with your friends and add other qualities.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. Accept reasonable qualities that fit each group.
Check your understanding
1. Physical features of Columbus – complete the table: physique, age, hair, complexion, face.
Physique: tall, well-built. Age: 46. Hair: prematurely white. Complexion: fair, almost ruddy. Face: melancholy when at rest.
2. Usually we sing songs to express joys and sorrows. Here the play begins with a song. What mood does this convey?
A rowdy, carefree and restless mood, which hints at discontent among the sailors.
3. ‘There are limits to patience,’ says Diego. What does this suggest about Diego’s state of mind?
Diego is impatient, frustrated and ready to rebel against the captain.
4. Who do you think has the lives of fifty in his hands? How?
Columbus. He is the captain of the ship, and the crew’s safety depends on his decisions.
Check your understanding
1. ‘A good sailor knows his place.’ Says Columbus to Diego. The statement is…
b. an indirect command.
2. Which reaction of Diego justifies your choice? Quote the phrase.
‘with repressed fury’ – Diego answers ‘Yes, sir’ but is clearly angry.
3. How does Pedro try to defend the drunken seamen? Was he right?
Pedro says they are simple men who need relaxation. He is partly right, since they need rest, but drinking on duty cannot be allowed.
4. What is termed as his worst enemy by Columbus?
His unbridled tongue.
5. The dialogue between Columbus and Pedro reveals this trait of Columbus.
b. quick temper.
6. Columbus is furious when he hears the song ‘Here’s a keg o’ rum’. What makes him react so?
The song mocks God – ‘The Devil laughs, but God is dumb’ – and so insults his faith and his mission.
Check your understanding
1. This section reveals the behaviour of … (fill in the blank)
Pepe – his loyalty and fearless devotion to Columbus.
2. Why do you think Pepe prefers to be in the company of Columbus?
Pepe admires Columbus and feels safe with him. He dislikes the seamen and finds them frightening.
3. Pepe is always eager to say that he is ever … to Columbus. (fill in the blank)
loyal (faithful, devoted).
4. Pepe warns Columbus about some people. Who are they?
The seamen (the crew) who are drunk and discontented.
Check your understanding
1. How are the seamen expressing their discontent even as Columbus can hear them?
By singing loudly, shouting and growling, which gets louder when Columbus orders them to stop.
2a. Pepe is heard saying, ‘They shan’t.’ Who are meant by ‘they’?
The seamen (the mutinous crew).
2b. What does the boy mean by saying ‘They shan’t’?
He means that the seamen will not be allowed to harm Columbus.
3. ‘The Santa Maria will be the lighter for his carcass.’ Whose words is Pepe quoting?
d. Guillermo Ires.
4. Which statement of Francisco suggests that he too has lost his temper? Quote his words.
‘Discipline is a thing of the past, sir.’
Check your understanding
1. ‘Who’s to put him in irons?’ challenges Guillermo. The person meant by ‘him’ is…
c. Columbus.
2. ‘I will perform it myself,’ says Columbus. What does ‘it’ mean here?
The duty of putting the mutinous man in irons (punishing him).
3. ‘Devil’s track to nowhere,’ says Guillermo. What does this suggest about the seamen’s thinking?
The seamen believe the voyage is pointless and dangerous, and that Columbus is leading them into disaster.
4a. After ‘a perceptible pause’, who grows more mutinous than others?
Diego.
4b. Quote his words.
‘Words for children! Froth and scum!’
Check your understanding
1. In his long speech, what does Columbus say he has discovered?
He has discovered that when a man is given a vision he must follow it alone, since loyalty, friendship and discipline do not last.
2. Pepe declares he is still loyal. What effect does it have on others like Juan and Guillermo?
They feel ashamed and sheepish. Guillermo slinks off, followed by others.
3. Compare Francisco’s confession with his earlier anger. How does Columbus react?
Earlier he said ‘Discipline is a thing of the past’; now he admits ‘desperate men do not always act up to the best that is in them’. Columbus responds with quiet irony.
4. How does Pedro react to Columbus’s sighting of a light?
He is excited and thankful, and says ‘Glory be to God!’
5. Do you consider the ending to be happy? Justify your answer.
Yes. Land is sighted and the crew is saved from a mutiny. Accept reasoned opposite views too.
Think about the text
1. ‘Mutiny is an ugly word,’ says Diego. Is mutiny an ugly word? Why?
Yes. Mutiny is a rebellion against the leader, which causes disorder and danger at sea.
2. What ‘will’ of God does Columbus want to fulfil through this venture?
To discover new lands, win new wealth for the King and Queen, and bring new souls to God.
3. Identify the mood of Columbus in saying ‘Would God implant the desire to solve mysteries and not provide the solutions?’
A puzzled, questioning and searching mood; he is uncertain, yet still hopeful.
4. Pepe says, ‘Everybody doubts… except me.’ Why is he an exception?
Pepe is a boy with pure faith and unquestioning loyalty to Columbus.
5. Why do the crew-mates of Columbus feel desperate?
They are far from home, tired of the long voyage without land, afraid of death and angry at Columbus’s strict discipline.
6. ‘Discipline knows no buts.’ Why is discipline needed in one’s life?
Discipline keeps order, helps people work together, and makes sure goals are reached safely.
7. Add more statements like ‘I am not ungrateful.’
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. ಮಾದರಿ: ‘I follow my vision alone.’ ‘I do not depend on the loyalty of others.’
8. ‘Shall simple men judge their betters?’ Share your opinion with your friends. (For / Against)
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು. Sample For: simple men have experience of the sea and common sense. Sample Against: they lack the vision and training of a leader.
9. How is the excitement of finding a new land expressed at the end?
Pedro: ‘It is, sir! Glory be to God!’ The sailor: ‘Blessed Mother of God! A light!’ and ‘Land! Land!’
10. ‘Your best cannot be bettered’, says Columbus. This implies that…
d. Columbus is not totally happy with Francisco (the remark is ironic).
11. Swami Vivekananda says purity, patience, perseverance and love are essential to success. Does Columbus possess all these qualities? Justify.
He shows patience and perseverance, but he lacks patience with his men and is quick-tempered, so he does not fully possess all of them.
12. Classify the words into Columbus (A) and mutinous sailors (B).
A (Columbus): short-tempered, authoritative, bold, farsighted, visionary. B (mutinous sailors): revolting, sheepish, ungrateful, silently angry, disloyal, submissive.

13. Fill in the blanks: This discovery, says Columbus, is a voyage of discovery. Apart from discovering the new land… depend on one’s faith… loyalty is as temporary as the sea weeds… discipline bursts… what remains is man in oneself… success to the blessings of God.
voyage; new land; faith; sea weeds; bursts; man; the end; God.

qb.q: What made Diego say that the life of fifty men was in the hands of Columbus?

qb.q: Columbus was always furious when he heard the seamen's song. Why did it make him furious?
qb.a: The song was over a cup of rum. It showed the despair of the seamen. They talked about God being dumb and doubted the success of the voyage. It voiced the pessimistic attitude of the seamen. So, Columbus was furious.

qb.q: Give a short description of the appearance of Columbus.
qb.a: Columbus was a tall, well-built man. His hair was prematurely white. He had a fair complexion.

qb.q: What does Columbus feel is his worst enemy? Why do you think he feels so?
qb.a: Columbus feels that his uncontrolled tongue is his worst enemy. Columbus was a man who soon lost his temper wouldget irritated quickly. He would often speak rudely to his men which made them angry towards him.

qb.q: How does Pedro try to defend the drunken seamen? Was he right in defending them?
qb.a: Columbus felt that the seamen were drinking too much. Pedro replied that they were simple men and wanted to relax by drinking They did not have the same vision as Columbus. Pedro was not right in defending the seamen because their drinking was leading to unruly behaviour.

qb.q: Whose company did Pepe prefer? What was the reason for this?
qb.a: Pepe preferred to be in the company of Columbus. Unlike the other seamen, he had faith in Columbus. He also felt that the others drank too much and behaved badly. So, he hated them.

qb.q: "Discipline knows no buts. What made Columbus say this?
qb.a: One of the seamen. Guillermo Ires, had disobeyed Columbus and spoken against him. Columbus wanted to punish him and so he ordered that Guillermo should be brought to him. Francisco refused to bring him. Columbus then said these words.

qb.q: How did the seamen show their anger towards Columbus?
qb.a: The seamen rushed towards Columbus, growling like wild animals. When Columbus shouted at them, they stopped but Guillermo Ires broke away from the others and moved forward to attack Columbus.

qb.q: What did Guillermo demand of Columbus?
qb.a: Guillermo was highly excited and shouted that they had suffered enough. Like other human beings, they too wanted to be in their homes with their families. He demanded that the Santa Maria should be turned back towards Spain at once.

qb.q: How did Pepe prove his loyalty to Columbus?
qb.a: Pepe had faith in Columbus. He warned Columbus to be careful about the desperate seamen. When the seamen rushed to kill Columbus, Pepe stood before them with his arms spread out and told them that they would have to kill him first. His loyalty put the others to shame.

qb.q: ‘This is a voyage of discovery.’ What had Columbus set out to discover?
qb.a: Columbus had set out to discover a new world, a beautiful land far away from Spain. This discovery would help to find new wealth and a new territory for his King and Queen to rule. When his men rebelled against him. Columbus said that he discovered one thing that if a manhad a vision, he must follow alone. He should not expect loyalty, friendship, discipline obedience from others.

qb.q: Columbus feels that whatever he does, it is God's will. What 'will' of God does he like to fulfil through this venture?
qb.a: Columbus felt that it was the will of God that he should discover new world which would bring wealth to his country and help them bring new souls on the path to God.Columbus had been sailing for many days and not yet sighted land. But, Columbus felt that if God had sent him, he would surely help him find a way.

qb.q: Usually, people feel desperate when they fail to get something they want. In the play, ‘The Discovery’, why do the crewmates of Columbus feel desperate?
qb.a: Columbus had told his men that they would discover a new world However, they had sailed for months and found nothing. They were tired and wanted to return to their homes. But Columbus would not give up. So, they were desperate.

qb.q: Swami Vivekananda says, "Purity, Patience and Perseverance are the essentials to success and above all love.’ Does Columbus possess all these qualities? Justify.
qb.a: Columbus had faith in God and there was purity in his intentions. All his men wanted to give up, but he had patience and he persevered till he reached his goal. He did not lose heart. Columbus had love for his country, love for God.

qb.q: Pepe says, "Everybody doubts…. except me." Why do you think he is an exception?"
qb.a: Pepe had faith in Columbus. Other sailors had no faith and belief in Columbus. Pepe was specially gifted and he stood with Columbus when other sailors revolted against him.

qb.q: Write an account of what the picture suggests to you, in a paragraph: (3 marks)
qb.a: The picture depicts a classic, dramatic scene of historical maritime exploration, capturing the pivotal moment a crew spots distant land. Standing on the elevated quarterdeck, a dignified captain—likely Christopher Columbus—holds a navigational tool while a young boy stands beside him, gazing out at the horizon. Below them, a visible cross-section of the ship shows the structured reality of life at sea: barrels packed tightly in the "Stores of Provisions," exhausted sailors resting in the "Seamen's Quarters," and muskets stacked in the "Weapon Armory." The true drama, however, unfolds on the main deck, where animated sailors point excitedly toward a faint break of light and land on the horizon under a stormy, cloud- filled sky, perfectly capturing the tension, relief, and profound sense of discovery at the end of a long voyage.

qb.q: "Columbus had a strong will, patience and perseverance." Justify the statement with examples.
qb.a: Columbus started his voyage with strong will of discovering a new world. When land was not sighted the seamen became desperate. They requested Columbus to take them back to Spain Columbus refused. Therefore the seamen under the leadership of Guillermo Ires revolted against him and tried to murder him. Guillermo called him a devil. He disobeyed his order and spoke against him. But Columbus withstood all the difficulties patiently He had patience and perseverance. He had learnt to face the brute. He was loyal to his king and queen. At last he was able to discover a new world.

qb.q: How can you say that Pepe was loyal to Columbus?
qb.a: Pepe was a page boy. He preferred the company of Columbus because he had faith in him. He did not like most of the seamen because they used to drink and revolt against Columbus. He warned Columbus to be careful about the desperate seamen. When other seamen doubted about the success of the voyage. Pepe was sure that Columbus would discover a new world. One day most of the seamen rushed towards Columbus like wild beasts to kill him. Pepe who was there stood before them with his arms spread and told them that they would have to kill him first. He was ready to sacrifice his life for his captain. His loyalty put the others to shame

qb.q: "Columbus was quite different from most of the seamen." Justify the statement with examples.
qb.a: Columbus had a vision. He had determined that he would not return to Spain till he discovered the new world. He thought that it was a God's will, he should do it. He set sail for a voyage on the Santa Maria to discover the new world. He and his 50 seamen sailed for many days but there was no sight of land. Many of his seamen became desperate, impatient and homesick. They asked Columbus to take them back to Spain. Columbus told them that he would not take them back to Spain till he discovered the new world. Guillermo, Diego and Francisco disobeyed his order. Guillermo said to Columbus“ I say the Santa Maria should turn her helm towards Spain at once or we are not men but sheep." Diego said, "Why should one man have the lives of 50 in his hands' Francisco refused to bring Guillermo to Columbus. Most of the seamen revolted and tried to kill Columbus. But Columbus was not afraid of their threats He told Guillermo that he should obey his order just as he obeyed his Royal Sovereign. In spite of their protests, he continued the voyage and discovered the new world in ice.

Check your understanding (Paragraphs 1–5)
1. Surender, a friend of Satish, came to visit him. Satish had not gone to school. Why?
Satish was unwell. He had terrible headaches and felt miserable since his last operation on his leg.
2. Identify the question that suggests Satish’s weakness. (Para 5)
‘But why are you speaking so softly? I can barely hear you.’
3a. Why was Satish confined to bed? (Para 12)
He was weak after the accident and the operations, and he suffered from frequent fevers and infections.
3b. What was the worst thing for him? Why was it so?
The silence was the worst. He could not hear the world around him, so everything seemed far away and like a silent pantomime. He could not talk or join in.
4. The school he was attending informed Satish’s father something. What was it?
The school said it could not keep Satish, because of his frequent absences and his hearing problem. He would have to look for a new school.
5. Satish didn’t want to go to a new school. What was the reason?
He did not want to go to a school where he could not talk to other children and where everyone would make fun of his deafness.
Check your understanding (Paragraphs 15–21)
1. After a lot of persuasion, Satish agreed to go to a new school. Do you think he was accepted?
No. The new school also refused him, saying it was for normal boys and suggesting a school for deaf and dumb children.
2. What made Avtar Narain angry? (Paras 15 and 16)
The headmaster bluntly told him to take his son to a school for deaf and dumb children.
3. The word ‘expedition’ in para 18 means: a) journey b) visit c) mountaineering
a) journey (a trip made with a purpose).
4. How did Satish’s brother Inder try to help him?
Inder sat with Satish for hours, talked to him, and taught him words and pronunciation.
5. Guess the meaning of these words from the context: snatches (Para 15), shattered (Para 18), brooded (Para 20), confined (Para 21). Verify with a dictionary.
snatches – parts or fragments of words; shattered – very upset and helpless; brooded – thought deeply and worried; confined – kept inside, restricted.
Check your understanding (Paragraphs 22–34)
1. What did Satish see in the far corner of the garden? Why did it attract him? (Para 22)
He saw a bird with a longish tail and a black crest. It attracted him because it was unlike any bird he had seen, and its restless energy fascinated him.
2. Both parents were his well-wishers, but each cared for him in a different way. How? (Paras 24, 25)

Father: stern and practical; he wanted Satish to study, read and earn a good career, so he took away the sketches. Mother: sympathetic; she asked why he was being denied his source of entertainment and felt for him.
3. Which action of Satish changed his father’s attitude? (Para 29)
Satish continued painting and drawing in spite of his father’s opposition, showing how much he loved art; his father saw him painting intently and realised how much it meant to him.
4. What was Satish unable to believe? (Para 30)
He could not believe that his father was not angry with him for painting.
5. How did Satish express his gratitude to his father? (Para 33)
He hugged his father tightly, filled with love for him.
Check your understanding (Paragraphs 35–38)
1. Name any three fields in which Satish Gujral made his name. (Para 35)
Painting, sculpture and architecture (he is also a writer).
2. How can you say Satish became popular all over the world? (Para 36)
His works have been exhibited all over the world and displayed in prestigious museums such as the Museum of Modern Art, New York.
3. Suggest another title for this story and justify your choice.

qb.q: Why had Satish not gone to school?

qb.q: How did Satish meet with an accident?
qb.a: During a holiday in Kashmir, Satish had gone hiking with his father and brother. As they were crossing a rickety bridge over some rapids, Satish looked down at the rushing waters. His foot slipped and he fell into the rapids.

qb.q: Why was Satish confined to bed? What was the worst thing for him? Why was it so?
qb.a: Satish was confined to bed because his legs remained weak even after getting healed. Moreover, he also suffered from bouts of fever and infections, especially of the ear. The worst thing for him was the silence which surrounded him. It was caused by medicines given to treat his leg.

qb.q: Many schools refused to take in Satish. How did it affect him?
qb.a: Many schools refused to take Satish in. This had a negative impact on him. Satish became very moody. He could not talk freely to others. He began to avoid going out to play.

qb.q: Why didn't Satish go to a new school?
qb.a: Satish did not want to go to a new school because he could not talk to other children and he thought everyone would make fun of his deafness.

qb.q: Why did Avtar Narain become angry with the headmaster?
qb.a: The headmaster refused to continue Satish in the school. He suggested Avtar Narain to take his son to the school for deaf and dumb children. This made Narain angry.

qb.q: How did Satish's brother Inder try to help him?
qb.a: Satish's brother Inder used to sit with Satish for hours and talked to him. He taught him words and their pronunciation.

qb.q: What effect did the books he read have on Satish?
qb.a: The books that Satish read were meant for older children or adults. They made him feel depressed and left a deep impression on his sensitive mind. He came to know that there was so much suffering in the world and he thought about this for long hours.

qb.q: Satish saw a bird through the window. How did the bird appear to him?
qb.a: It was a beautiful bird with a longish tail and black crest. It was energetic. Its eyes kept moving here and there and its whole body seemed ever ready for flight.

qb.q: At the beginning, Avtar Narain did not like his son's love for painting. Why?
qb.a: Avtar Narain did not like his son's love for painting at the beginning because he believed that artists were paid less. Their allowances were insufficient and so they lived in poverty. He did not feel it to be a good carrier for a bright boy.

qb.q: Both the parents were his well wishers. But each cared for him in a different way. How?
qb.a: Satish's father wanted him to gain a lot of knowledge. So, he bought many books for him to read. His mother, on the other hand, was a soft-hearted lady who felt that he should be allowed to do painting, if he was happy, doing so.

qb.q: Which action of Satish changed his father's attitude?
qb.a: Satish's father did not approve of Satish keeping himself busy with painting. But Satish did not stop doing it. One day, Satish was mixing colours on a palette and his father didn't say anything to him. He rather put his hand on Satish's shoulder as if encouraging him. Satish was unable to believe that his father was not angry with him for painting.

qb.q: How did Satish express his gratitude to his father?
qb.a: Satish's eyes filled with tears when he saw that his father had brought colours, brushes and rolls of drawing sheets for him. He took a step forward and hugged his father tightly to show his love and gratitude to him.

qb.q: Why is Satish Gujral popular all over the world?
qb.a: Satish Gujral is one of the few accomplished artists who is famous in several art forms like painting, sculpture and architecture. He is also a writer.

qb.q: "Satish became a great artist." What makes you appreciate him?
qb.a: Satish Gujral is among the foremost artists in India, excelling in painting, sculpture and architecture. Exhibitions of his work have been held all over the world. He is also a writer and has published books of his works in the various arts. From his life, we learn that physical disability is no barrier to success.

qb.a: The silence was the worst thing for Satish. He felt as if some huge weight was pressing upon his head making everything seem far away and silent. qb.q: What was Satish unable to believe about his father?
qb.a: Satish was unable to believe that his father was not angry with him for painting. Whenever Satish involved himself in drawing and painting, his father never encouraged him. But for the first time, his father placed his hand on Satish's shoulder, which made Satish realize that his father had finally accepted and appreciated his interest in drawing and painting.

qb.q: Name any three fields in which Satish Gujral has made his name.
qb.a: Satish Gujral has made his name in several fields of arts likepainting,sculpture and architecture.

qb.q: Name the prestigious museums that have exhibited Gujral's artworks.
qb.a: Satish Gujral’s artworks have been exhibited in prestigious museums like the Museum of Modern Art, New York, the Hiroshima Collection, Washington and the National Gallery of Modern Art,New Delhi.

qb.q: How did Satish meet with an accident?
qb.a: When on a holiday in Kashmir, Satish was hiking with his father and brother. They were crossing a rickety bridge over some rapids. Satish looked down at the swirling water below him. His foot slipped. He lost his balance and fell into the rapids. As a result of this, his legs were injured. His legs became weak. He suffered frequentbouts of fever and infections. He could not hear properly. The headmaster did not allow him to come to school because he was hard of hearing and frequently absent for the class. His father tried to get admission for him in some other school, but in vain. Satish felt that children would tease him. Therefore, he was compelled to stay at home.

qb.q: Everything seemed like scenes from some pantomime show to Satish. Why?
qb.a: When Satish went to Kashmir with his family, he fell into rapids and got fractured. He suffered from frequent fever and infections, especially of the ear. He felt as if some huge weight was pressing upon his head, making everything seem far away and silent. He felt helpless and upset at being confined to bed as he was. The silence was the worst for Satish. Everything seemed like scenes from pantomime show as he was slowly losing his hearing capacity.

qb.q: How was the accident during a vacation, a turning point in Satish's life?
qb.a: Satish met with an accident and lost his sense of hearing and was also sick for a long time. He could not go to school. His father was more interested in sending his son to school to get him educated. In the beginning he was not happy with his son's paintings. But as he was deaf for life he could not attend the normal school so he began to do painting. But later on when his father encouraged his son's talent and nurtured it he became a great artist of India. Satish Gujral is among the foremost artists of India and accomplished in several art forms like painting, sculpture and architecture.

qb.q: How did the bird inspire Satish to become an artist?
qb.a: A beautiful sight of a bird changed Satish’s life. One day, Satish saw a rare bird which had a long tail, a black crest and moving eyes. It was an active bird. For a long time, he stared at it. Then he took out his notebook and pencil and began sketching the bird from his memory, with a few deft strokes. That day, he had discovered another pastime which he could indulge in. He began filling pages of his notebook with doodles. This incident, lead Satish to become one of the greatest artists of India.

qb.q: How can we say that Satish Gujral became popular with the able support of his father?
qb.a: Despite his physical disability, Satish Gujral became a great artist. He worked hard to reach that feat. Due to an accident, he lost his hearing. He was refused admission in normal schools. One day he saw a beautiful bird. That made him to take interest in painting and drawing. Later, his father admitted him in one of the best art schools. Today, he is among the foremost artists of India. He is an architect, painter, sculptor, and writer. His works are exhibited all over the world. He was awarded the Order of the Crown for the best architectural design of the Belgium Embassy in New Delhi. His work has been exhibited all over the world and displayed in various museums like the Museum of Modern Art, New York, the Hiroshima collection, Washington and the National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi. He has published four books on his works in various arts. He has also been honoured with the Padma Vibhushan. His achievementsshow that ‘Physical Disability is no Barrier to Success’.

qb.q: Explain the struggles faced by Satish after the accident.
qb.a: Satish had to face many struggles after the accident. His legs were plastered, his head was badly injured and he suffered injuries all over his body. His legs remained weak and required several operations. He sufferedfrequently from fever and infections, especially of the ear. He felt as if a huge weight was pressing upon his head, making everything seem far away and silent.Being confined to bed, Satish felt helpless and upset. The silence was the worst part for him. Everything seemed like scenes from some pantomime show. He wanted to scream and break the silence, but he could not. For an eight-year-old boy, this was a truly terrible experience.

qb.q: How did books influence Satish's sensitive mind?
qb.a: Satish’s father believed that reading and education were the keys to success. While Satish was bedridden, his father provided him many books. When Satish started reading books, another world opened out for him.He became a voracious reader.Some books were all serious works meant for older children and even for adults.They made him feel depressed and left a deep impression upon his sensitive mind. He came to know of another world which is full of suffering and anguish.He brooded long and hard about why there was so much suffering in the world while his own world looked comfortable in comparison.

lessons.words: camaraderie – friendship when people work together; promotion – move to a more important position; overwhelming – a very strong feeling; annihilation – complete destruction; retaliation – action against someone who has harmed you; ominous – suggesting something bad will happen; acronym – a word formed from the first letters of other words (e.g. MAD); standoff – a situation in which neither side can gain an advantage; violate – go against an agreement; survival – continuing to live or exist; Iron Curtain – the border between Western Europe and the communist countries of Eastern Europe; obvious – clear, indisputable; persistent – continuing; self-criticism – judging one’s own behaviour; lore – knowledge about a subject; immersion – being absorbed in an activity; fundamental – most basic; forensic – relating to scientific methods of solving crimes; headhunt – find people with the right skills; trigger – cause something to happen quickly; trillion – a very large number; stalemate – a situation with no agreement possible; springboard – something that helps one start; venture – a new activity that involves risk; indispensable – very useful and necessary; doze – sleep lightly; solitary – alone; confinement – being kept in a place; gaol – prison; capsule – part of a spacecraft that separates; centre of gravity – the point where weight acts; tracking – following; trans-galactic – across galaxies
lessons.notes: Keilis-Borok – a Russian scientist who worked on seismic waves; Leo Tolstoy – Russian writer of ‘War and Peace’; Frank Press – American scientist; Cold War – unfriendly relations between the USA and the Soviet Union after the Second World War; Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD) – the idea that both sides would be destroyed in a nuclear war; Geneva – the place of the technical meeting; McGeorge Bundy – US National Security Advisor to two presidents; Norman Nicholson – an English poet from the Cumberland coast.
