3. How is ‘MAD’ a paradox? How could MAD affect the superpower nations?

MAD stands for Mutually Assured Destruction. It seems strange because the threat of destruction is what keeps the peace. It pushed the superpowers to avoid a first strike and to seek agreements such as the test ban.
4. What was the problem the nuclear powers faced? Was it the violation or its detection?
The problem was detection: how the others could find out if one power had secretly carried out an underground nuclear explosion.
5. Why were the technical experts summoned by the three superpowers?
To solve the problem of detecting secret underground nuclear tests, so that a nuclear test ban could be enforced.

In the survival of humankind, by using the theory of seismic waves to tell natural earthquakes from nuclear explosions.
7. Why was it outwardly difficult for the two sides of the Iron Curtain to find a solution?
Because of Cold War tensions and the differences in their cultural backgrounds.
8. How are scientists able to work in spite of political and cultural differences?
They shared a common language based on respect for hard evidence, ranking by expertise alone, and persistent self-criticism.

Scientists around the world think and work in the same way, so one never feels lonely abroad; there is hope for survival and well-being while there is science; scientists can agree despite cultural differences.

Antibiotics, electronics, biotechnology, synthetic fibres, the green revolution and genetic forensic diagnosis all came from fundamental research.

People trained in theoretical physics are headhunted by financial institutions, and those trained in biological research become founders and directors in the pharmaceutical industry, because their knowledge is valuable.

qb.a: i) Once upon a time, in a forest, there lived three friends - two geese and a tortoise. There was a severe drought.Scarcity of food and water became a challenge for the inhabitants. The three friends decided to migrate to a different place in search of food. The two geese could fly, but the tortoise couldn't. The friends thought of a plan to carry the tortoise with them. They held a stick with their beaks, and the tortoise held the middle of the stick with its mouth. The geese flew, carrying the tortoise, and as they soared through the sky, some children below clapped at the sight. The tortoise, feeling insulted and got angry, burst out, "Whose idea was this?". Unfortunately, as soon as the tortoise spoke, it lost its grip on the stick and fell onto a rock, dying instantly. The moral of the story is that sometimes, it's better to keep quiet and not boast or seek unnecessary attention, as it can lead to one's downfall. ii) Once, a lion was asleep in the forest. A little mouse began running up and down on the lion's body, awakening him. The lion caught the mouse and was about to eat it when the mouse cried, "Pardon, O King!" The lion, being kind, lifted his paw and let the mouse go. Sometime later, a few hunters captured the lion and tied him to a tree. The little mouse happened to pass by and saw the lion's predicament. The mouse gnawed through the ropes, freeing the lion. The lion was grateful to the mouse for saving his life. The moral of this story is one should never underestimate others based on their size or strength. Kindness and gratitude can lead to unexpected friendships and assistance in times of need.

qb.q: Write an essay on any one of the following: ( 4 marks) a) Ban on Plastic b) Internet c) National Festivals d) Advantages and disadvantages of AI.
qb.a: i) Ban on Plastic Plastic things are integral part of human being. We have been using plastic day-to-day for many reasons. We use plastic bags, plastic container, plastic bottles, plastic toys and so on. These are cheaply available in the market. All of these do make our lives easier. But the more we use plastic and dispose of it into the environment, we are facing more risks. There are numerous reasons to ban plastic. Some of these includes Plastics are non-biodegradable. Thus, disposing them of is the biggest challenge. Waste plastics are polluting the land and water. Plastics have become a threat to the life of animals living on earth as well as in water. Chemicals released by waste plastics enter the soil and make it infertile. Plastics lead to drainage problem. Burning plastic causes air pollution. Plastics are a major cause of environmental pollution. It is necessary to ban plastics before they ruin our planet completely. We, the educated should control the use of plastic bags. Instead of using plastic bags we should use eco- friendly alternatives to plastic bags. We should carry cloth bags. We should spread awareness about the harmful effects of plastics. The government has taken many measures to ban single use plastics. However, the implementation of this rule is yet to reach perfection. We should remember to Reduce, Refuse, Reuse and Recycle plastics. “Think green. Avoid plastics” ii) Internet Today the Internet is the most powerful tool in the world. The Internet is a collection of various services and resources. However, like every single innovation in science and technology, Internet has played an important part in our daily life, The foremost target of Internet has always been the communication. We can avail the facilities of email; we can chat for hours with our friends. With the help of such services, it has become very easy to establish a kind of global friendship where you can explore other cultures of different countries. Information is the biggest advantage internet is offering. The Internet is a virtual treasure of information. Any kind of information on any topic is available on the Internet, Entertainment is another popular reason explaining why many people prefer to surf the Internet. Downloading games and songs, visiting chat rooms or just surfing the web are some of the pleasures people have discovered. Students have also benefitted immensely with the use of internet. In case any of their lectures gets missed in the class, Internet has all the required information. Online coaching has also benefitted the students who do not have access to good educational institutes in their area for the preparation of competitive exams such as JEE and NEET, etc. Apart from those advantages, Internet also has some disadvantages; Misuse of internet can spoil our life. These days the teenagers are found addicted to internet as they spend most of their time in internet playing online games, surfing social networking sites etc. As a result, they are lagging behind in their study. On the other hand, lots of people have become the victim of cybercrime. Some anti-social group use internet to deceive people through cheat-funds. Hackers may easily access our personal information that has been stored in internet. There are a host of games that are available on the internet and this has made most children to shun all outdoor activity. Internet acquaints us with the latest happenings around the world. Internet has made our lives extremely comfortable as well as interesting. Nowadays we can’t live without Internet. iii) National Festivals: Indian National festivals like Independence Day, Republic Day, and Gandhi Jayanthi play a vital role in uniting the nation. They remind citizens of India's rich history, struggles for freedom, and the values of democracy and non-violence. These festivals foster patriotism, cultural pride, and a sense of belonging among Indians. Independence Day : Independence Day celebrates India's freedom from British rule in 1947. It's a day of pride, reflecting on the sacrifices of freedom fighters. The Prime Minister hoists the flag at the Red Fort, and citizens across the country celebrate with flag-hoisting, parades, and cultural events. Republic Day : Republic Day marks the adoption of India's Constitution in 1950. It's a celebration of India's transition to a democratic republic. The President unfurls the flag at Rajpath, New Delhi, with grand parades showcasing India's diversity, military strength, and cultural heritage. Gandhi Jayanthi : Gandhi Jayanthi honours Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary. It's a day to reflect on his principles of non- violence, truth, and simplicity. People pay tribute through prayer meetings and events promoting peace and community service, keeping Gandhi's ideals alive. d) Advantages and Disadvantages of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a technology that enables machines to perform tasks that usually require human intelligence. It is widely used in education, healthcare, business and many other fields. AI has several advantages. It can work quickly and accurately, saving both time and effort. AI-powered systems help doctors diagnose diseases, assist students in learning, and improve productivity in workplaces. It can also analyse large amounts of data and provide useful information for better decision-making. AI- based devices such as virtual assistants and navigation systems make daily life easier and more convenient. However, AI also has some disadvantages. One major concern is unemployment, as machines may replace workers in certain jobs. Developing and maintaining AI systems can be expensive. AI also raises privacy concerns because it often collects and stores personal information. Another limitation is that AI lacks human emotions, creativity, and moral judgment. It can make mistakes if it is given incorrect or biased data. In conclusion, AI is a powerful technology that offers many benefits, including efficiency, accuracy, and convenience. However, it also presents challenges such as job loss and privacy issues. Therefore, AI should be used wisely and responsibly to ensure that it benefits society while reducing its negative effects.
